Step 1: Extract descriptions exactly from input that describe the goods.  
- "These charms are thin"  
- "they will work great as charms"  
- "maybe a bit big"

Step 2: Filter negative descriptions from step 1.  
(Note: No clearly negative descriptions — “maybe a bit big” is a mild qualifier but not negative in context, so all are kept.)  
- "These charms are thin"  
- "they will work great as charms"  
- "maybe a bit big"

Step 3: Filter descriptions like "looks like picture", "looks like photo".  
(Not present.)  
- "These charms are thin"  
- "they will work great as charms"  
- "maybe a bit big"

Step 4: Filter descriptions unrelated to color/shape/material/size/pattern/usage scenario/style.  
- "These charms are thin" → related to material/thickness (keep)  
- "they will work great as charms" → usage/general function → too general (remove)  
- "maybe a bit big" → related to size (keep)  

Remaining:  
- "These charms are thin"  
- "maybe a bit big"

Step 5: Convert each description into adjective phrase.  
- "These charms are thin" → "thin charms"  
- "maybe a bit big" → "somewhat large"

Step 6: Shorten each adjective phrase as short as possible.  
- "thin charms" → "thin"  
- "somewhat large" → "large"

Step 7: Filter general adjective phrases like "nice", "great", "good", etc.  
("thin", "large" are specific, not general like "nice" or "great")  

Final result:  
thin, large
